summary: Adds an indexed notifications.conversation_id column (migration backfills it from the JSON data in 500-row batches; an observer fills it for new notifications) and makes opening a conversation mark that user's notifications read by exact conversation_id instead of a slow LIKE on the JSON data, which also stops e.g. conversation 12 marking conversation 123's notifications read.

statements.why: Route still behind $this->middleware('auth') + authorize('viewCached') (ConversationsController.php:38,48); query is scoped to the logged-in user's notifications; no data loss.

statements.text: 1. Apply 2026_08_28_010101_add_conversation_id_column_to_notifications_table to your live database before the new code goes live (`php artisan migrate --force`), or the parts that use it will fail.
statements.why: Without the column, opening any conversation (where conversation_id query) and creating any notification (observer sets conversation_id) would hit SQL errors.

misses.what: Card never says what changed: opening a conversation now marks its notifications as read using a new indexed column (faster), and no longer wrongly marks notifications of conversations whose number starts with the same digits (e.g. #12 vs #123).

The migration backfills every existing notification row one by one after a full LIKE scan; on large help desks the update/migration can take a long time, during which the new code fails if it is already live.
